name: Dock Order History Product Restrictions for WooCommerce
author: Jacek Sultan

sections.description:
Dock Order History Product Restrictions for WooCommerce hides selected products and product categories from customers until they have completed a required number of orders in your store.

Pick the products or categories you want to protect, set how many orders are needed, and choose which order statuses count. Customers who do not qualify never see the restricted products in listings, search results or product recommendations, and direct links are blocked as well.

Useful for:

  • VIP and members-only products
  • loyalty programs and customer rewards
  • wholesale access after a first paid order
  • hidden product catalogs

Features:

  • Restrict entire WooCommerce product categories
  • Restrict individual products
  • Require a minimum number of orders
  • Choose which order statuses grant access
  • Hide restricted products from shop and category pages
  • Hide restricted products from search results
  • Hide restricted products from related, cross-sell and up-sell blocks
  • Block direct product and category URLs with a redirect or a 404 page
  • Built-in access test for any user account
  • WooCommerce HPOS compatible
  • AJAX product and category selectors
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Upload the plugin.
  3. Activate the plugin.
  4. Go to WooCommerce > Product Access Rules.
  5. Select products or categories.
  6. Define the required order count.
sections.faq:
Can I restrict only one product?

Yes. Products can be selected individually.

Can I restrict an entire category?

Yes. All products assigned to selected categories will be restricted.

What order statuses are counted?

You can select which WooCommerce statuses should grant access.

What happens when a blocked customer opens a restricted URL?

You choose between a redirect to the My Account page and a 404 page.

How do I check the rules for a single customer?

The settings screen includes an access test. Enter a user ID and the plugin reports whether that account currently has access.

Is WooCommerce HPOS supported?

Yes.
